about.title: About
btn.hint: “Terminate” asks the process to close cleanly. If that does not help after 5 s, “Kill now” is highlighted. Both ask for confirmation first.
confirm.kill_text: Kill {name} (PID {pid}) now? The process cannot close cleanly anymore, and unsaved data is lost.
confirm.terminate_text: Ask {name} (PID {pid}) to terminate? Unsaved data in this process may be lost.
confirm.title: Terminate process?
detail.none_selected: No process selected. Click a process on the left.
error.runtime_missing: orbitop needs the package {package}. Install it with: sudo apt install {package}
hint.igt_missing: intel_gpu_top is not installed. Without it, orbitop shows only the Intel graphics usage of your own processes.
hint.igt_noperm: No permission to run intel_gpu_top. Please run scripts/setup-privileges.sh.
hint.nvsmi_missing: nvidia-smi is not installed. Without it, NVIDIA graphics values are not shown.
hint.rapl_noperm: CPU package power is not readable. It can be enabled with setup-privileges.sh --allow-rapl. Risk: the counters then become readable for all programs, which is a side channel.
legend.busy_iounknown: Like “constant load, no I/O”, but the I/O of a foreign process cannot be checked. A hint, not a verdict: it may well be reading or writing.
legend.busy_noio: Almost 100% of one core for over 2 minutes, without reading, writing or waiting. A hint, not a verdict: this can be an endless loop or a long calculation.
legend.kernel_hang: Stuck in a kernel operation for over 10 s, usually disk, USB or a network drive. This is a real hang. Even “Kill now” only takes effect once the kernel releases it.
legend.stopped: Has been paused, for example with Ctrl+Z. It can be resumed.
legend.title: What the states mean
legend.waiting: Sleeping and waiting for input, network or a timer. Normal. Limit: a program that has blocked itself internally (deadlock) looks exactly the same from outside. For windowed programs, GNOME reports this itself with “not responding”.
legend.working: Computing or reading and writing, and the values keep changing. Normal.
legend.zombie: Has already exited, only the entry is left. It cannot be terminated; it disappears with its parent process.
result.denied: Termination was not permitted (cancelled or no permission).
result.kernel: Kernel threads and PID 1 cannot be terminated.
result.mismatch: The PID now belongs to a different process. Nothing was terminated.
result.nohelper: Terminating other users' processes needs the helper installed by sudo bash scripts/setup-privileges.sh.
result.sent: Termination requested. Checking in 5 s whether the process is still running.
result.zombie: A zombie cannot be terminated. It disappears with its parent process.
verdict.busy_iounknown: Constant load, I/O could not be checked. It has been computing non-stop on one core for {since}. Whether it reads or writes could not be checked, because it is a foreign process. That can be an endless loop or a long calculation. Are you expecting it to compute for this long?
verdict.busy_noio: Constant load with no sign of life from outside. It has been computing non-stop on one core for {since}, reads and writes nothing and waits for nothing. That fits an endless loop, but just as well a long calculation. From outside the two cannot be told apart. Are you expecting it to compute for this long?
verdict.kernel_hang: Stuck in the kernel. It has been stuck in a kernel operation for {since}, usually disk, USB or a network drive. This is a real hang. Even “Kill now” only takes effect once the kernel releases it.
verdict.stopped: Stopped. The process has been paused, for example with Ctrl+Z. It can be resumed.
verdict.waiting: The process is waiting for input, network or a timer. This is normal.
verdict.working: The process is working. It is computing or reading and writing, and the values keep changing. This is normal.
verdict.zombie: Zombie. The process has already exited, only the entry is left. It cannot be terminated and disappears with its parent process {parent}.
